BREAKFAST
# Belgian Waffles

Makes: 6 waffles


Ingredients
• 2 cups flour
• 4 tsp baking powder
• 1/2 tsp salt
• 1/2 cup sugar
• 2 eggs, separated
• 1/2 cup vegetable oil
• 2 cups milk
• 1 to 2 tsp vanilla

Instructions
1. Sift (optional) the dry ingredients into a large bowl, then mix.

2. In a separate bowl, beat the egg whites until stiff peaks form.

3. In another bowl, mix the vanilla, milk, egg yolks and oil.

4. Combine the wet ingredients with the dry ingredients, leaving out the whites.

5. Fold in the whites until just combined.

6. Cook in the waffle maker on medium for 2 to 3 minutes, then raise the heat and cook until the
steam stops. Keep an eye on it so it doesn't burn.

Tried and True Recipes 3

BREAKFAST
# Homemade Cinnamon Rolls

Prep: 30 min
Cook: 22 min
Rise: 1 hr 10 min
Total: 1 hr 59 min
Makes: 12 rolls


Ingredients
Dough
• 1 cup warm milk (about 115°F)
• 2 1/2 tsp instant dry yeast (Red Star Platinum recommended)
• 2 large eggs, room temperature
• 1/2 cup salted butter, barely melted or softened (not hot)
• 4 1/2 cups all purpose flour, divided
• 1 tsp salt
• 1/2 cup granulated sugar

Filling
• 1/2 cup salted butter, almost melted
• 1 cup packed brown sugar
• 2 tbsp cinnamon
• 1/2 cup heavy cream (poured over the risen rolls)

Frosting
• 6 oz cream cheese, softened
• 1/3 cup salted butter, softened
• 2 cups powdered sugar
• 1/2 tbsp maple extract (or vanilla)

Instructions
Make the Dough
1. Pour the warm milk into the bowl of a stand mixer and sprinkle the yeast over the top.

2. Add the eggs, butter, salt and sugar.

3. Add 4 cups of the flour (save the last 1/2 cup in case you need it) and mix with the beater blade just
until barely combined. Let it rest 5 minutes so the flour soaks up the liquid.

4. Switch to the dough hook. Beat on medium, adding up to 1/2 cup more flour if needed, and knead 5
to 7 minutes until elastic and smooth. The dough should be tacky and still stick to the sides of the
bowl. That's fine, don't add more flour.

5. Oil a large bowl, place the dough inside, cover lightly and let it rise somewhere warm for about 30
minutes. Too much rising makes the rolls airy.

Fill and Shape
6. In a medium bowl, mix the soft butter, brown sugar and cinnamon until well combined.

Tried and True Recipes 4

7. Flour your surface and rolling pin and roll the dough into roughly a 24 x 15 inch rectangle. It doesn't
have to be exact.

8. Spread the filling over the whole surface. Don't skip the edges.

9. Roll up tightly (hot dog style), cut into 12 pieces, place in a pan and let rise until doubled.

Bake
10. Preheat the oven to 375°F.

11. Warm the heavy cream until lukewarm and pour it evenly over the risen rolls.

12. Bake at 375°F for 20 to 22 minutes, until lightly golden and the center rolls are cooked through. Time
varies with roll size and quantity.

Frost
13. Beat the cream cheese, butter, powdered sugar and extract with a hand mixer until smooth.

14. Spread over the cooled rolls. Store in an airtight container.

Tried and True Recipes 5

APPETIZERS
# Spinach Puffs

Oven: 450°F
Bake: 20 min


Ingredients
• 2 to 3 cups spinach, roughly chopped
• 3 tbsp dill, finely chopped
• 1 shallot, finely minced
• 3 large cloves garlic, crushed
• Olive oil
• Salt and pepper
• 2 eggs, separated
• 4 oz full fat cream cheese
• 1/2 cup feta cheese
• 2 to 4 oz parmesan, grated
• 2 to 3 slices bacon, finely chopped
• 1 package puff pastry

Instructions
Filling
1. Rinse the spinach, remove the stems and chop into small bite sized pieces. Finely chop the dill and
mince the shallot.

2. Heat olive oil in a pan over medium high. Cook the shallot about 2 minutes until translucent, then
add the garlic for about 30 seconds until fragrant.

3. Add the spinach with a pinch of salt and cook it down. Add the dill, sauté briefly, then add some
fresh pepper. Remove from heat.

4. In a mixing bowl, combine the cream cheese, feta and parmesan. Stir in the spinach mixture, the
bacon and one egg yolk.

Assemble and Bake
5. Preheat the oven to 450°F.

6. Flour your surface well and lay out the puff pastry. Roll lightly to remove creases, cut into 3 to 4 inch
squares and place on a parchment lined baking sheet.

7. Spoon about 2 tbsp of filling onto each square. Beat an egg and brush two edges of each square,
then fold and crimp the egg washed edges together. (Playing '80s power ballads is strongly
encouraged.)

8. Chill the whole tray in the fridge for 10 minutes. Brush each pastry with egg wash and bake 20
minutes, rotating the pan at 10 minutes.

9. Cool on a wire rack, then serve.

Tried and True Recipes 6

MAINS
# Pizza Dough

Prep: 15 min
Rise: 30 min
Cook: 15 min
Total: 1 hr
Makes: One 10 to 12" pizza


Ingredients
• 2 to 2 1/3 cups all purpose or bread flour, divided (250 to 295 g)
• 1 packet instant yeast (2 1/4 tsp)
• 1 1/2 tsp sugar
• 3/4 tsp salt
• 1/8 to 1/4 tsp garlic powder and/or dried basil (optional)
• 2 tbsp olive oil, plus more for the bowl and crust
• 3/4 cup warm water (175 ml)

Instructions
1. In a large bowl, combine 1 cup (125 g) flour, the yeast, sugar and salt. Add garlic powder and basil
now if using.

2. Add the olive oil and warm water and stir very well with a wooden spoon.

3. Gradually add another 1 cup (125 g) flour, stirring until the dough forms a cohesive, elastic ball that
pulls away from the bowl. It will be slightly sticky but manageable.

4. Generously oil a separate large bowl and brush oil up the sides.

5. With lightly floured hands, shape the dough into a ball, place it in the oiled bowl and roll it around
until coated. Cover tightly with plastic wrap and set somewhere warm.

6. Let rise 30 minutes or until doubled. If baking right away, preheat the oven to 425°F (215°C) now.

7. Gently deflate the dough, move it to a lightly floured surface and knead briefly (3 to 5 times) until
smooth.

8. Shape into a 12 inch circle by hand or with a rolling pin. Move to a parchment lined pizza pan and
pinch or fold the edges into a crust.

9. Brush the whole surface, crust included, with about 1 tbsp olive oil. Poke holes all over the center with
a fork so it doesn't bubble.

10. Add toppings and bake at 425°F (215°C) for 13 to 15 minutes until golden. Slice and serve.

Tip: All purpose flour gives a softer crust. Bread flour gives a slightly crispier one.

Tried and True Recipes 7

MAINS
# Cheese Pizza

Makes: One 10 to 12" pizza


Ingredients
• Pizza dough (see Pizza Dough)
• Pizza sauce, any kind
• Olive oil or butter
• Cheese: mozzarella and provolone preferred, sliced or shredded
• Vegetable toppings (optional)
– Onion
– Pepper
• Hot pepper flakes
• Herbs
– Basil
– Oregano
• Protein toppings, cooked first (optional)
– Chicken
– Hot dogs
– Lunch meats

Instructions
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F with a heavy pan, pizza stone or skillet inside. Not required, but it cooks
the pizza faster and better.

2. Roll the dough into a circle and thicken or roll the edges into a crust if you like. If the dough keeps
shrinking back, let it rest 10 to 15 minutes to relax the gluten, then keep rolling.

3. Spread the sauce evenly over the dough.

4. Add your vegetables or meats, then the cheese on top.

5. Sprinkle red pepper flakes on top if desired.

6. Brush the crust with butter or olive oil and drizzle a little olive oil over the pizza.

7. Bake on the hot pan for 13 to 15 minutes, until the crust is browned and crispy and the cheese is
melted, bubbling and browned.

8. Cool a few minutes, then slice and serve hot.

Tried and True Recipes 8

MAINS
# Spaghetti and Chicken Meatballs

Meatballs: 40 to 60 min
Sauce: 2 hrs
Pasta: 10+ min
Serves: 4 or more


Ingredients
Meatballs
• 1 lb ground chicken
• 1/2 to 1 tsp garlic
• 1/2 tsp dried marjoram
• 1/2 tsp dried thyme
• 1/2 tsp dried basil
• 1/2 tsp dried oregano
• 1/3 cup bread crumbs or panko
– Half regular, half Italian seasoned
• 1 egg, beaten
• 1 tsp salt
• 3/4 tsp ground black pepper
• 1/4 cup grated parmesan
• Olive oil for frying

Tomato Sauce
• 5 lb tomatoes, fresh or frozen
• 3 tbsp olive oil
• 2 medium onions, chopped
• 4 cloves garlic, minced
• 1 tsp each dried basil, oregano, thyme and marjoram
• 2 tsp salt
• 1 tsp ground black pepper
• 1 tsp or more sugar (optional)

Pasta and Serving
• Spaghetti
• Salt and olive oil
• Grated parmesan for topping

Instructions
Meatballs
1. Combine the chicken with all the other meatball ingredients (except the oil) and mix thoroughly by
hand.

2. With wet hands, form into balls of your preferred size and set on parchment paper.

Tried and True Recipes 9

3. Heat olive oil in a large, wide pan over medium heat.

4. Cook the meatballs until the bottoms are golden brown, then turn until most or all sides are
browned.

5. Drain on a paper towel lined plate.

Tomato Sauce
6. Peel and core the tomatoes, saving the juices.

7. In a pot, sauté the onions in oil until just browned. Add the garlic and cook about a minute until
fragrant.

8. Add the tomatoes and seasonings, bring to a boil, then simmer 1 to 1.5 hours.

9. Blend smooth with an immersion blender.

10. Taste and adjust salt, pepper and sugar. Add heat if you like.

Pasta
11. Bring a pot of water to a boil and salt it generously.

12. Cook the pasta until al dente or your preferred doneness, then drain.

13. Return it to the pot, toss with a little olive oil so it doesn't stick and cover until ready.

Bring It Together
14. Simmer the meatballs in the sauce, covered on low, for 45 minutes or more.

15. Reheat the pasta, plate it with sauce and meatballs and top with grated parmesan.

Tried and True Recipes 10

MAINS
# Sauerkraut with Sausage

Serves: 4 to 6


Ingredients
• 2 lb sauerkraut, juice and cabbage separated
• 1/2 to 1 lb sausage
• 2 onions, chopped
• 4 cloves garlic, chopped
• 2 tbsp butter
• 1 tbsp oil
• 30 g mushrooms, fresh or dried, chopped
• 1 tsp coarsely ground caraway seeds
• 1 tbsp paprika
• 2 bay leaves
• 1/2 tsp peppercorns
• 4 quarts water (or more)

Instructions
1. Rinse the sauerkraut once or twice, then squeeze it out. Save the juice separately.

2. Melt the butter and oil in a large pot, cook the onions until golden, then add the garlic for about 1
minute until fragrant.

3. Add the sausage, cut into medium pieces, and sauté until lightly browned and the juices start to
release.

4. Add the caraway, paprika, bay leaves and peppercorns.

5. Immediately add the sauerkraut.

6. Add the water. Use less for a thicker dish, more for a soupier one.

7. Add the sauerkraut juice a little at a time until it's just below the sourness you want.

8. Add the chopped mushrooms.

9. Simmer about 45 minutes, until the cabbage is soft. Taste for sourness and salt, adjust and serve
hot.

Tried and True Recipes 11

DESSERTS
# Perfect Pie Crust
Enough for a bottom and top crust.

Prep: 1 hr 15 min
Makes: 2 crusts


Ingredients
• 2 1/2 cups all purpose flour, plus extra for rolling
• 1 cup unsalted butter (2 sticks), very cold, cut into 1/2 inch cubes
• 1 tsp salt
• 1 tsp sugar
• 6 to 8 tbsp ice water

Instructions
1. In a food processor, pulse the flour, sugar and salt to mix.

2. Add the butter half at a time, pulsing until crumbly.

3. Add ice water one tablespoon at a time until the dough barely comes together. It should hold its
shape when squeezed between your fingers.

4. Turn the crumbly mixture out onto a clean, dry surface and gather into a mound. Divide into two
equal mounds.

5. Knead each mound just enough to form a disk with no cracks. Don't over knead. That builds gluten
and makes the crust tough. Small flecks of butter in the dough are good: they become flaky layers.

6. Dust each disk with flour, wrap in plastic and refrigerate at least 1 hour or up to 2 days.

Tried and True Recipes 12

DESSERTS
# Apple Pie

Oven: 425°F, then 350°F
Bake: 50 to 60 min


Ingredients
• Pastry for a 9 inch double crust pie (see Perfect Pie Crust)
• 1/2 cup unsalted butter
• 3 tbsp all purpose flour
• 1/2 cup white sugar
• 1/2 cup packed brown sugar
• 1/4 cup water
• 1 tsp cinnamon
• 1/4 tsp ginger
• 1/4 tsp nutmeg
• 8 Granny Smith apples, peeled, cored and sliced
• Egg white, for brushing

Instructions
1. Preheat the oven to 425°F. Grease a pie pan and lay the bottom crust in it.

2. In a large, wide pot, melt the butter and stir in the flour to form a paste.

3. Add the sugars, water, cinnamon, nutmeg and ginger. Heat and stir until smooth, then add the
apples and cook until tender but not mushy. Cover to steam them faster; if there's too much liquid,
cook uncovered to reduce it.

4. Fill the pie with the apples, add the top crust in any design you like and brush with egg white for
shine.

5. Bake 14 minutes at 425°F, then lower to 350°F and bake 35 to 45 minutes more, until the top is
golden and darkened but not burnt.

6. Let rest 10 minutes, then serve with ice cream.

Tried and True Recipes 13

DESSERTS
# Chocolate Lava Cake
Molten, decadent and easy. The ultimate treat for chocolate lovers.

Recipe by John Kanell

Prep: 10 min
Cook: 10 min
Total: 20 min
Makes: 6 cakes
Calories: 381 each


Ingredients
• 1/2 cup unsalted butter
• 6 oz bittersweet chocolate
• 2 eggs
• 2 egg yolks
• 1/4 cup sugar
• 1 pinch salt
• 2 tbsp flour
• Powdered sugar and berries, for garnish (optional)

Instructions
1. Preheat the oven to 450°F. Butter and flour your ramekins.

2. Melt the butter and chocolate together on low heat in a double boiler or the microwave. Whisk until
smooth.

3. In a medium bowl, beat the eggs, egg yolks, sugar and salt until thick and pale. An electric mixer
works best.

4. Fold the chocolate mixture and flour into the eggs. Pour into the ramekins and bake at 450°F for 6 to
8 minutes, longer or shorter depending on how much lava you want and your oven.

5. Let cool in the ramekins for 1 minute. Cover each with an upside down dessert plate, carefully flip,
wait 10 seconds and lift off the ramekin.

6. Dust with powdered sugar, add berries if you like and serve immediately.

Tried and True Recipes 14

DESSERTS
# Chocolate Chip Cookie Brownie Skillet

Prep: 10 min
Cook: 30 to 35 min
Oven: 350°F
Serves: 16


Ingredients
Brownie Batter
• 1/3 cup butter, melted
• 1/2 cup brown sugar
• 1/4 cup white sugar
• 1/3 cup unsweetened cocoa powder
• 1 large egg
• 1 tsp pure vanilla extract
• 1/2 tsp salt
• 1/4 cup all purpose flour

Cookie Dough
• 1/4 cup butter, softened
• 1/4 cup light brown sugar
• 1/4 cup granulated sugar
• 1 large egg
• 1 tsp pure vanilla extract
• 2/3 cup all purpose flour
• 1/8 tsp baking soda
• Pinch of salt
• 1/3 cup dark or semi sweet chocolate chips

Instructions
Prep
1. Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Lightly grease a 9 inch cast iron skillet or round pan with spray,
butter or oil.

Brownie Batter
2. In a medium bowl, whisk the melted butter and sugars until the sugar dissolves. Whisk in the cocoa
until smooth.

3. Beat in the egg and vanilla (about 1 minute). Fold in the flour and salt until smooth and thick. Set
aside.

Cookie Dough
4. In another bowl, beat the butter and sugars until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg and vanilla until
smooth.

5. Fold in the flour, baking soda and salt until a dough forms. Fold in half the chocolate chips.

Tried and True Recipes 15

Assemble and Bake
6. Spread the brownie batter evenly in the skillet. Scoop the cookie dough on top and sprinkle with the
remaining chips.

7. Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until the cookie is golden and the edges are set and pulling away from the
pan. Don't overbake or it'll be dry instead of fudgy.

8. Cool in the pan about 10 minutes and serve warm.

Tip: Natural granulated sweetener can replace the sugars to cut calories.

Tried and True Recipes 16

DESSERTS
# Chocolate Chip Cookies

Chill: 2 hrs to overnight
Oven: 325°F
Bake: 12 to 13 min
Makes: 16 large cookies


Ingredients
• 2 1/4 cups (280 g) all purpose flour, spooned and leveled
• 1 tsp baking soda
• 1 1/2 tsp cornstarch
• 1/2 tsp salt
• 3/4 cup (170 g) unsalted butter, melted and slightly cooled
• 3/4 cup (150 g) packed light or dark brown sugar
• 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar
• 1 large egg + 1 egg yolk, room temperature
• 2 tsp pure vanilla extract
• 1 1/4 cups (225 g) semi sweet chocolate chips or chunks

Instructions
1. Whisk the flour, baking soda, cornstarch and salt together in a large bowl. Set aside.

2. In a medium bowl, whisk the melted butter, brown sugar and granulated sugar until no lumps
remain. Whisk in the egg, then the yolk, then the vanilla.

3. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and mix with a large spoon or spatula. The dough will be very
soft but thick.

4. Fold in the chocolate. It may not stick well because of the melted butter; do your best.

5. Chilling is mandatory. Cover and refrigerate 2 to 3 hours or up to 3 to 4 days. Overnight gives the
least spreading.

6. Let the dough soften at room temperature for 10 minutes.

7. Preheat the oven to 325°F (163°C). Line two large baking sheets with parchment or silicone mats.

8. Roll into balls of about 3 tbsp each. The dough will be crumbly but your hands will warm it together.
Shape them taller than wide so the cookies bake up thick.

9. Place 8 balls per sheet. Press a few extra chips on top for looks if you want.

10. Bake 12 to 13 minutes. They'll look very soft and underbaked; they keep baking on the sheet.

11. Cool on the sheet 10 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool completely.

Tip: Covered at room temperature, cookies stay fresh up to 1 week.

Tried and True Recipes 17

DESSERTS
# Crème Brûlée
Per single serving. Multiply for as many ramekins as you need.

Oven: 250°F
Bake: 45 min
Serves: 1


Ingredients
• 1 egg yolk
• 1 tbsp sugar
• 1/2 tsp vanilla
• Heavy cream to bring the total to 1/2 cup
• Extra sugar and a little honey, for the topping

Instructions
1. Preheat the oven to 250°F.

2. Mix the egg yolk and sugar with a fork until well combined.

3. Add the vanilla, then the cream, and mix gently. Don't let it get frothy.

4. Pour into a ramekin of about 5 oz.

5. Bake about 45 minutes, until it jiggles like Jell-O when lightly tapped.

6. Chill completely in the fridge.

7. In a small pot, cook 1 to 2 tsp sugar per serving with a drop of honey and water until bubbly and
browned to your liking.

8. Pour over the custard and tilt the ramekin to spread the topping evenly.

9. Let it set, then serve at room temperature or cold.

Tried and True Recipes 18
